UnitStatement: Repo-native skills are reusable method packs that a bounded Type 2 agent may load at runtime.
Skills are not agents and do not have their own decision rights, write scopes, or interaction surfaces.
A skill method bundle states the task shape it supports.
A skill method bundle states which tools are preferred or allowed.
A skill method bundle states which runtime overrides matter.
A skill method bundle states what outputs should exist.
A skill method bundle states how to QA the run.
AGENT_TASK.md is the canonical loader for repo-native skills.
SKILLMAKER owns skill design, contract evolution, and subsystem governance.
Skill outcomes must conform to HELPS_HUMANS R10, HELPS_HUMANS R12, and the Design Outcomes for Skill Contracts section.
A new skill is appropriate when the role stays the same but the method and toolchain vary.
A new skill is appropriate when write authority is supplied by the bounded TASK brief and the interaction model stays the same.
A bounded task should not become a new agent merely because it has a different tool recipe.
When TASK loads a skill, human instructions in the run brief have highest precedence.
The TASK shell hard authorization boundary takes precedence over the skill contract.
Skill defaults have lower precedence than the skill contract.
A skill must never widen write authority beyond the TASK shell and effective bounded task brief.
When a persona agent dispatches TASK with TaskSkill, TASK automatically loads the skill's SKILL.md and companion files.
Skill hydration guarantees the worker receives the full contract without the orchestrator reconstructing it in the dispatch prompt.
SKILL.md is the authoritative method and output contract for a skill.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md defines the dispatch contract for invoking a skill through TASK.
TOOL_POLICY.md defines the tool allowlist and preferences for a skill.
QA_CHECKS.md defines output validity checks for a skill.
RuntimeOverrides supply runtime parameters, and CustomInstructions supply run-specific reinforcement.
CustomInstructions do not replace the skill contract.
Each skill must live in its own folder under skills/<skill_name>/.
Each skill folder must include SKILL.md, BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md.
Skill folders may include optional extras such as examples, notes, and helper templates for humans.
Every SKILL.md should include YAML frontmatter with at least name and description.
Every SKILL.md should state the skill purpose and suitable task shapes.
Every SKILL.md should state required inputs and optional runtime overrides.
Every SKILL.md should state output expectations, TASK safety, and important non-negotiable constraints.
The frontmatter is the portable discovery surface for a skill.
The Markdown body is the Chirality execution guidance for a skill.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md are required Chirality-specific companion files layered on the core skill contract.
Skills may reference deterministic tools under tools/ by policy, not by hidden assumption.
Good skill design makes preferred tools explicit.
Good skill design makes disallowed tools explicit.
Good skill design states when to fall back from tools to manual or LLM reasoning.
Briefs and skills are orthogonal.
A task brief provides run-specific authority, scope inputs, write permissions, overrides, and expected outputs.
A skill provides the method pack for a recurring task shape.
The metadata.chirality-task-profile frontmatter field should normally be NONE.
Non-NONE metadata.chirality-task-profile values are deprecated compatibility metadata, not write-scope grants.
deliverable-consistency should normally begin with tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py, then read only flagged files and nearby context.
PDF2MD dispatches TASK + pdf2md-page for text transcription.
When PDF2MD uses ASSET_MODE=prose, it dispatches TASK + pdf2md-page-assets for page-bounded figure, table, and image discovery.
PDF2MD deterministic tools materialize crops and CSVs, anchor page Markdown, aggregate the public asset manifest, and validate references.
DBM_PUBLISHER first runs deterministic section mapping and section context packet generation.
DBM_PUBLISHER dispatches TASK + dbm-section-publish once per approved publication section with its read-only context packet.
DBM_PUBLISHER dispatches TASK + dbm-publish for package assembly, knowledge coverage and open-items records, and content adequacy.
After DBM package assembly, TASK + dbm-postauthor-concordance builds a post-authoring evidence bundle for human disposition.
TASK + dbm-concordance-verify may provide optional semantic cross-section consistency observations.
DBM publication skills remain publication-local and should be confined to _Publication/DBM/ scopes rather than mutating KTY-local truth.
WORKING_ITEMS dispatches TASK + dbm-draft-review to review a human-prepared draft DBM against the governed knowledge base.
dbm-draft-review runs scan_section_coverage.py, extract_claims.py, scan_tbd_markers.py, and check_body_thinness.py as deterministic substrate tools.
dbm-draft-review uses agent judgment to compare substrate against governed truth and prepare candidate findings.
The human dispositions dbm-draft-review findings through the REVIEW agent.
dbm-concordance-seed is legacy and is no longer dispatched by DBM_PUBLISHER.
Concordance has moved from the pre-authoring gate to post-authoring evidence bundle review.
Agents must treat skills/ as a live skill root rather than relying on hard-coded skill lists in narrative documents.
Each immediate subfolder of skills/ that contains SKILL.md is a repo-native skill.
Agent guidance says to read skills/README.md first for the shared contract.
When a specific skill is requested, the agent should inspect SKILL.md, BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md in that skill folder.
Agents should use the live skills/ folder rule for skill counts and use AGENTS.md plus tools/REGISTRY.md for indexes.
Agents should not assume another document's embedded skill list is current.
If live folder contents and a canonical index disagree, agents must surface the discrepancy explicitly.
A well-bounded and auditable TASK run with a skill, scope, and tool permissions should probably be a skill rather than a new top-level agent.
For new skills, the TaskSkill token should match the skill folder and name frontmatter exactly.
New skill names should prefer lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only.
After adding or renaming skills, run tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py on skills.
validate_skill_metadata.py scans every immediate skill folder under skills/.
validate_skill_metadata.py validates both the basic authoring contract and the machine-consumed runtime contract.
The basic authoring contract includes name, description, folder alignment, and required TOOL_POLICY.md presence.
The machine-consumed runtime contract includes metadata.chirality-* values, canonical allowed-tools syntax, and tool-path resolution under tools/.
The skill template is used when creating a new repo-native skill under skills/.
Skill contracts conform to AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS design outcomes for skill contracts and compliance requirements R10 plus R12.
AGENT_SKILLMAKER owns skill contract evolution and subsystem governance.
New skills must pass tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py.
The skill template frontmatter includes name, description, optional compatibility, optional allowed-tools, and chirality metadata.
The skill template sets metadata.chirality-skill-version to "1" and metadata.chirality-task-profile to NONE.
A skill Purpose section states the recurring bounded task the skill supports.
A skill Suitable agent shells section lists TASK and any optional brief-shape constraints.
A skill Inputs section distinguishes required and optional fields.
A skill Runtime overrides section records each key's meaning, default, and allowed values.
A skill Tool usage section lists preferred tools and optional tools when applicable.
A skill Tool usage section lists disallowed tools.
A skill Outputs section lists expected artifacts.
A skill Non-negotiable constraints section records constraints.
A skill QA expectations section records checks.
Every skill must include BRIEF_SCHEMA.md.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md documents the dispatch contract for invoking the skill through TASK.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md must document required brief fields, optional fields, RuntimeOverrides guidance, and recommended CustomInstructions content.
CustomInstructions in a brief carry run-specific reinforcement and do not replace SKILL.md.
Every skill must include TOOL_POLICY.md.
Implicit tool assumptions are a design defect.
TOOL_POLICY.md uses canonical section headings for Preferred tool order, Allowed deterministic tools, Expected use of reasoning, Disallowed use, and Write boundary.
The Allowed deterministic tools section uses TASK-enforced and Operationally invoked H3 subsections.
Every TOOL_POLICY.md must include Allowed deterministic tools, Disallowed use, and Write boundary.
Preferred tool order and Expected use of reasoning may be skipped when no content applies.
Every skill must include QA_CHECKS.md.
QA_CHECKS.md documents minimum output validity checks, failure reporting expectations, and required evidence or logs.
The allowed-tools frontmatter field is machine-consumed by TASK during skill resolution.
allowed-tools must be a comma-space-delimited list of command specs.
Each allowed-tools command spec has the form <interpreter> <repo-relative-tool-path>:<scope_glob>.
allowed-tools specs cannot include flags, extra arguments, or commas inside a spec.
The interpreter token in an allowed-tools spec is a single token such as python3.
The repo-relative-tool-path token in an allowed-tools spec is a single token relative to repo root.
The scope_glob follows the final colon in an allowed-tools command spec.
If allowed-tools is malformed, TASK rejects the skill with an error.
The allowed-tools field should be omitted entirely when a skill has no deterministic tool requirements.
A skill folder name should be the TaskSkill token used in briefs.
The name frontmatter should match the skill folder name.
Skill folder names should prefer lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens.
After creating or updating a skill, run python3 tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py skills.
validate_skill_metadata.py checks all skill folders under skills and does not target one named skill unless given a narrower root.
BRIEF_SCHEMA defines the INIT-TASK dispatch contract for TASK + content-digest.
content-digest is used when EVALUATION needs one structured digest for one deliverable folder.
ScopePath should normally be the execution root for a content-digest run.
AllowedWriteTargets should be limited to the intended digest output path under _Evaluation/content-digests/.
The PURPOSE brief field states why a digest run exists.
The ScopePath brief field identifies the execution root.
The TaskSkill brief field must equal content-digest.
AllowedWriteTargets lists the digest output path for the run.
RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH identifies the target deliverable folder.
RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH identifies the digest output file.
ExpectedOutputs lists the expected single digest file.
content-digest defines no optional runtime overrides.
DELIVERABLE_PATH must identify exactly one deliverable folder.
OUTPUT_PATH must already have an existing parent directory under _Evaluation/content-digests/.
The content-digest run must remain single-deliverable and read-only on production files.
A valid content-digest run writes exactly one digest file to OUTPUT_PATH.
The digest must contain all seven required sections in the required order.
Identity fields must come from _CONTEXT.md or be explicitly marked absent.
Dependency counts and key upstream or downstream items must be derived only from deliverable-local files.
Quality observations must be specific factual flags rather than vague judgments.
A content-digest run must not modify any file in DELIVERABLE_PATH.
A content-digest run must not read any file outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest reports FAILED_INPUTS when DELIVERABLE_PATH is missing or is not a directory.
content-digest reports FAILED_INPUTS when the parent directory of OUTPUT_PATH does not exist.
Absent deliverable-local files do not fail the run by themselves and are reported as missing in the digest.
content-digest reads one deliverable folder and produces a structured seven-section content digest.
The content digest summarizes identity, scope, document kit, dependencies, references, semantic framework, and quality observations.
content-digest is a bounded semantic-matching extraction skill.
content-digest reads deliverable-local files and extracts structured information directly.
content-digest does not perform engineering judgment or cross-deliverable analysis.
Each content-digest invocation is dispatched by EVALUATION with a brief specifying the deliverable path and output location.
Each content-digest invocation produces one digest file.
content-digest uses the TASK generic shell mode with no profile.
The typical content-digest dispatcher is EVALUATION, batched by package with one dispatch per deliverable.
ScopePath is a required input and is set to the execution root.
AllowedWriteTargets is a required input for the execution-root _Evaluation/content-digests/ location.
RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH is a required absolute path to the deliverable folder.
RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH is a required absolute path to the digest output file.
DEL-ID is derived at runtime from _CONTEXT.md or inferred from the deliverable folder name.
DEL Name is derived at runtime from _CONTEXT.md.
PKG-ID is derived at runtime from _CONTEXT.md.
content-digest has no optional runtime overrides.
DELIVERABLE_PATH must be a valid directory path containing _CONTEXT.md.
OUTPUT_PATH must be under _Evaluation/content-digests/{PKG-ID}/ with an existing parent directory.
content-digest reads are limited to files within the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest reads _CONTEXT.md in full for identity, description, acceptance criteria, and scope traceability.
content-digest reads _DEPENDENCIES.md in full for tracking mode, upstream/downstream summary, and register statistics.
content-digest reads _REFERENCES.md in full for source document pointers.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Datasheet.md for key parameters and structured metadata.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Specification.md for requirements and scope definition.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Guidance.md for design rationale, principles, and considerations.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Procedure.md for execution workflow.
content-digest reads only the first 40 lines of _SEMANTIC.md for framework type and perspective.
content-digest must not read outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest must not cross into adjacent deliverable folders or scan package-level or project-level registers.
content-digest writes are limited to exactly one file at RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH.
The parent directory of OUTPUT_PATH must already exist, and content-digest does not create it.
content-digest uses no deterministic tools.
content-digest is a reasoning-first, semantic-matching extraction skill.
content-digest intentionally omits the allowed-tools frontmatter field.
content-digest must not write outside OUTPUT_PATH.
content-digest must not modify any file in DELIVERABLE_PATH.
content-digest must not read files outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest must not perform cross-deliverable scanning or comparison.
The precondition step validates that DELIVERABLE_PATH exists and is a directory.
If DELIVERABLE_PATH is not a directory, content-digest reports RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS.
The precondition step validates that the parent directory of OUTPUT_PATH exists.
If OUTPUT_PATH has no existing parent directory, content-digest reports RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS.
content-digest reads each file listed in the read boundary while respecting its read scope.
If a read-boundary file is absent, content-digest records that fact and does not fail.
content-digest extracts package, discipline, type, and responsible identity fields from _CONTEXT.md.
content-digest extracts description, acceptance criteria, SOW traceability IDs, and objective traceability IDs from _CONTEXT.md.
content-digest extracts a one-sentence focus summary for Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure.
content-digest extracts tracking mode, upstream count, downstream count, key upstream, and key downstream from _DEPENDENCIES.md.
content-digest extracts the list of all referenced documents from _REFERENCES.md.
content-digest extracts whether _SEMANTIC.md is present and the framework type if identifiable.
content-digest scans read content for TBD items and their resolution authority.
content-digest scans read content for ASSUMPTION labels and their rationale.
content-digest scans read content for placeholder text or incomplete sections.
content-digest scans read content for Conflict Table entries with HumanRuling status.
content-digest scans read content for enrichment markers such as A-001 and B-001.
content-digest scans read content for inconsistencies between documents within the folder.
content-digest quality observations are factual flags, not evaluative judgments.
content-digest writes the structured digest to OUTPUT_PATH using the defined seven-section structure.
content-digest overwrites the digest file if it already exists.
The digest file contains exactly seven sections in order.
The digest Identity section includes package, discipline, type, and responsible fields.
The digest Scope section includes description, acceptance criteria, SOW traceability, and objective traceability.
The digest Document Kit Summary section includes Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure focus summaries.
The digest Dependencies section includes tracking mode, upstream count, downstream count, key upstream, and key downstream.
The digest References section lists all referenced documents.
The digest Semantic section states whether _SEMANTIC.md is present and gives the framework type if identifiable.
The digest Quality Observations section lists TBDs, placeholders, and inconsistencies with IDs where available.
Missing information is noted as not present or TBD in source.
The digest output must not leave placeholder braces in the file.
content-digest outputs one digest file at RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH containing the seven required sections.
content-digest is read-only on deliverable production documents.
content-digest processes exactly one deliverable folder per run.
content-digest reports what source files contain and does not infer, speculate, or fill gaps.
content-digest marks missing information explicitly.
content-digest uses semantic matching rather than deep reasoning.
content-digest flags quality observations without performing engineering judgment.
content-digest produces one digest per run.
content-digest preserves the seven-section structure in the specified order.
EVALUATION_REPORT, not content-digest, is responsible for evaluative assessment of deliverable correctness.
content-digest QA expects all seven sections to be present in the output digest.
content-digest QA expects identity fields to be populated from _CONTEXT.md without invention.
content-digest QA expects SOW and OBJ traceability IDs to be listed or explicitly marked absent.
content-digest QA expects dependency counts to be stated with key upstream and downstream items named.
content-digest QA expects quality observations to be specific items with IDs where available.
content-digest QA expects no files in DELIVERABLE_PATH to be written or modified.
content-digest QA expects the digest to be written to the specified OUTPUT_PATH.
content-digest QA expects no files outside the deliverable folder to be read.
EVALUATION synthesizes content-digest outputs across packages.
EVALUATION_REPORT applies evaluative reasoning when scoring dimensions.
content-digest does not perform scoring or cross-deliverable synthesis.
content-digest first reads the bounded deliverable-local files listed in the skill contract.
content-digest then uses direct reasoning to extract and summarize structured information into the seven-section digest.
TASK enforces no deterministic tools for content-digest.
No deterministic tools are operationally invoked by content-digest.
content-digest performs bounded extraction and summarization only.
content-digest identifies quality-observation signals from deliverable-local files without crossing into engineering judgment or cross-deliverable synthesis.
content-digest tool policy disallows writes outside OUTPUT_PATH.
content-digest tool policy disallows modification of files in DELIVERABLE_PATH.
content-digest tool policy disallows reading files outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest tool policy disallows cross-deliverable scanning or comparison.
content-digest may write exactly one file at RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH.
The dbm-concordance-seed brief schema defines the INIT-TASK dispatch contract for TASK + dbm-concordance-seed.
The dbm-concordance-seed skill is used by DBM_PUBLISHER for bounded reasoning over an approved section, small section group, or strong-model consolidation scope.
The dbm-concordance-seed skill transforms raw evidence atoms into typed concordance candidates before the blocking register is frozen.
The brief ScopePath should normally be the publication planning folder under _Publication/DBM/_Planning/.
The brief AllowedWriteTargets must name exactly two files.
One allowed write target is a scope-local concordance candidate CSV.
One allowed write target is a scope-local concordance seed QA markdown file.
The brief must not grant write access to section output folders, package folders, or KTY-local source folders.
The TaskSkill field in the brief must equal the skill folder name dbm-concordance-seed.
CONCORDANCE_SCOPE_ID is the stable identity for the seeding scope.
CONCORDANCE_SCOPE_MODE states whether the run covers one section or a group.
SECTION_IDS lists the approved section IDs in scope.
EVIDENCE_ATOMS_PATH points to raw evidence atoms from deterministic extraction.
RISK_INVENTORY_PATH points to the mechanical risk inventory to cover or waive.
CANDIDATE_OUTPUT_PATH identifies the scope-local refined candidate output.
SEED_QA_OUTPUT_PATH identifies the scope-local QA output.
PUBLICATION_INPUT_MANIFEST identifies the frozen input manifest.
PUBLICATION_SCHEMA_PATH identifies the approved publication schema.
SECTION_MAP_PATH identifies the approved section map.
PUBLICATION_RULES_PATH identifies the approved publication rules.
MAX_KA_FILES_TOTAL is the hard cap on total mapped KAs for the scope.
CANDIDATE_INPUT_PATH may provide an optional draft candidate input for consolidation or rerun passes.
PUBLICATION_CONCORDANCE_REGISTER_PATH may provide an existing frozen register for reruns or expansion passes.
HYPERGRAPH_USE_MODE states whether hypergraph evidence is admitted for the run.
CONCORDANCE_SCOPE_MODE should normally be SINGLE_SECTION unless DBM_PUBLISHER deliberately groups tightly coupled sections.
SECTION_IDS must match approved section IDs present in Section_Map.csv.
CANDIDATE_OUTPUT_PATH and SEED_QA_OUTPUT_PATH must both live under _Publication/DBM/_Planning/.
PUBLICATION_CONCORDANCE_REGISTER_PATH is optional because the initial seed pass may run before the blocking register exists.
EVIDENCE_ATOMS_PATH and RISK_INVENTORY_PATH are required for all new hardened publication runs.
CANDIDATE_INPUT_PATH is optional for strong-model consolidation or reruns over draft candidates.
Candidates from smaller-model over-collection must remain NEEDS_REVIEW until consolidated.
MAX_KA_FILES_TOTAL should reflect the approved bounded-scope design, not an ad hoc worker preference.
CustomInstructions should be used only for run-specific reinforcement.
CustomInstructions must not recreate the skill contract because TASK hydration loads the authoritative contract.
A dbm-concordance-seed run is valid only when both required outputs exist.
All dbm-concordance-seed writes must stay inside approved _Publication/DBM/_Planning/ paths named in the brief.

The candidate CSV must contain required typed columns including AssertionDomain, DiscoverySource, SourceKTYIDs, SourceSectionIDs, NormalizationHint, NormalizationContract, Criticality, ComparisonParameter, SourceFidelityCritical, and SourceExpectedValue.
Every emitted candidate row must tie to at least one approved section through AuthoritySectionID, RequiredSectionIDs, or SourceSectionIDs unless ResolutionStatus is OUT_OF_SCOPE.
AssertionKey values must be stable uppercase snake case and must not encode ad hoc section-local prose.
Unsupported or ambiguous candidates must remain explicit as NEEDS_REVIEW, DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE, or OUT_OF_SCOPE.
New candidate additions must be grounded in mapped source content and must not rely on non-authoritative roots such as _MEMORY.md or _SEMANTIC.md.
The QA artifact must use the required stable block structure in the required order.
Every READY_FOR_FREEZE candidate must have a non-empty NormalizationContract.
Every concordance-relevant SOURCE_AUTHORITY evidence atom must have SourceFidelityCritical set to YES and a populated SourceExpectedValue.

The concordance seed QA artifact must contain the H2 headings Scope Summary, Inputs Consumed, Candidate Refinements, New Candidate Additions, Ambiguities Requiring Review, Duplicate / Merge Notes, and Normalization Guidance in order.
The Inputs Consumed QA block records the candidate input path, planning artifacts consulted, sections covered, and mapped source inputs materially used.
The Candidate Refinements QA block records existing candidate rows that were materially completed or corrected.
The New Candidate Additions QA block records genuinely added candidates and their engineering rationale.
The Ambiguities Requiring Review QA block records unresolved authority ownership, semantic duplication, or normalization uncertainty.
The Duplicate / Merge Notes QA block records rows that look semantically related but were not safely merged.
The Normalization Guidance QA block records how later section workers should normalize comparison values consistently.
The candidate output CSV must include AssertionKey through ResolutionStatus columns listed in the required schema.
Allowed ResolutionStatus values are READY_FOR_FREEZE, NEEDS_REVIEW, DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE, and OUT_OF_SCOPE.
Criticality must be one of HIGH, NORMAL, or LOW.
DiscoverySource must record whether the row came from structured data, prose extraction, open issues, decision log, scope change, or another approved source class.
ComparisonParameter must be populated when ComparisonRule requires extra rule detail such as rounding precision.
SourceKTYIDs and SourceSectionIDs must identify the mapped source and support footprint for the row.
NormalizationHint must be present whenever a later section worker could normalize the same value in multiple valid ways.
NormalizationContract must be present for READY_FOR_FREEZE rows.
SourceFidelityCritical=YES rows must include SourceExpectedValue or remain NEEDS_REVIEW.
FAILED_INPUTS is used when required runtime overrides are missing, output paths are outside planning, section IDs mismatch, mapped KA count exceeds the cap, or required artifacts are missing.
FAILED is used when a required output cannot be written despite valid inputs or an internal run error prevents stable output emission.
Even successful runs must surface unresolved authority ownership, duplicate candidates, normalization ambiguity, material dependencies, and deliberately OUT_OF_SCOPE candidates.
The dbm-concordance-seed skill metadata declares chirality-skill-status as LEGACY.

The dbm-concordance-seed skill transforms raw concordance evidence atoms into typed publication concordance candidates for one approved section, bounded section group, or strong-model consolidation pass.
The deterministic tool produces raw evidence atoms with provenance and mechanical risk signals.

The dbm-concordance-seed skill owns concordance relevance, type and domain classification, criticality assessment, authority section selection, comparison rule selection, normalization contract population, and source-fidelity designation.
The skill consumes frozen publication planning artifacts plus evidence atoms and the risk inventory.
The skill reads only mapped publication inputs for its assigned scope.
The skill emits one scope-local typed candidate CSV and one scope-local seed QA markdown file.
The dbm-concordance-seed skill is not a section writer, package gate, or dispatcher.
The suitable agent shell for dbm-concordance-seed is TASK generic shell mode with no profile.

Required dbm-concordance-seed inputs include scope identity, scope mode, section IDs, evidence atoms, risk inventory, candidate output, QA output, publication manifest, publication schema, section map, publication rules, and MAX_KA_FILES_TOTAL.
Optional dbm-concordance-seed inputs include candidate input, concordance register path, source domain, prose-only discovery flag, strict section matching flag, and hypergraph-related paths or modes.
CONCORDANCE_SCOPE_MODE allows SINGLE_SECTION or SECTION_GROUP.
CANDIDATE_OUTPUT_PATH must be under _Publication/DBM/_Planning/.
SEED_QA_OUTPUT_PATH must be under _Publication/DBM/_Planning/.
MAX_KA_FILES_TOTAL must be a positive integer.
HYPERGRAPH_USE_MODE may be NONE, AUXILIARY_PLANNING, AUXILIARY_QA, or AUXILIARY_PLANNING_AND_QA.
The dbm-concordance-seed skill is reasoning-first.
The skill consumes deterministic candidate input produced upstream instead of invoking publication tools itself.
The skill has no deterministic tool requirement of its own.
The skill must not dispatch other skills or agents.
The skill must not mutate frozen planning artifacts except for the two scope-local outputs named in the brief.
The skill must not directly freeze Publication_Concordance_Register.csv.
The skill must not modify CAT, KTY, or KA input files.
The skill must not use _Aggregation, _Coordination, _Evaluation, _Reconciliation, _MEMORY.md, or _SEMANTIC.md as factual authority, except admitted hypergraph evidence when enabled.
When the skill reads _STATUS.md, it must also read sibling _MEMORY.md as non-authoritative operational context when present.
The skill must not guess assertions unsupported by explicit mapped content.
Hypergraph evidence may suggest candidates but cannot supply assertion values.
The skill output paths are CANDIDATE_OUTPUT_PATH and SEED_QA_OUTPUT_PATH.
The authority hierarchy starts with approved Publication_Schema.md.
Approved Publication_Rules.md is second in the authority hierarchy.
Approved Section_Map.csv is third in the authority hierarchy.
An existing Publication_Concordance_Register.csv is fourth in the authority hierarchy when provided.
Current evidence atoms and risk inventory are fifth in the authority hierarchy.
The frozen Publication_Input_Manifest.md is sixth in the authority hierarchy.
Accepted scope-change state and approved decomposition state named in the manifest are seventh in the authority hierarchy.
Exact mapped KTY-local files named by the section map are eighth in the authority hierarchy.
Vocabulary map, open-issues register, and decision log named in the manifest are ninth in the authority hierarchy when required for typing, normalization, or state selection.
Original or reference markdown and provenance tables are reference and provenance only and do not override accepted DOMAIN, SCA, or mapped CAT/KTY/KA-local content.
Hypergraph evidence is auxiliary structure evidence only.
Hypergraph evidence does not replace the content authority hierarchy.
When planning-mode hypergraph inputs are provided, the skill may use hypergraph evidence to suggest repeated-value or assertion clusters.
When planning-mode hypergraph inputs are provided, the skill may use hypergraph evidence to identify additional participant sections.
When planning-mode hypergraph inputs are provided, the skill may use hypergraph evidence to identify likely missing concordance candidates implied by graph adjacency.
The skill must not invent assertion values from graph topology.
The skill must not prefer graph structure over mapped CAT/KTY/KA-local content when they conflict.
A candidate discovered or strengthened by hypergraph evidence must use DiscoverySource=HYPERGRAPH_AUXILIARY.
The seed QA output should note hypergraph-influenced candidates and the structural pattern that motivated them.
Every emitted candidate row must preserve or fill the typed concordance fields listed by the skill.
NormalizationContract is a machine-readable normalization specification for section workers.
NormalizationContract examples include ROUND_N:2, TOKEN_MATCH, EXACT, RANGE_MATCH, and SET_MATCH.
SourceFidelityCritical is YES when a key represents a value that should be checked against admitted reference or provenance material at Gate 6.

SourceFidelityCritical=YES applies to equipment counts, specification values, scope inclusion or exclusion decisions, and values whose unexplained source-publication divergence would be material error.
SourceFidelityCritical=NO applies to structural or organizational keys without a direct reference counterpart.
SourceExpectedValue is the normalized expected value from admitted reference or provenance material when SourceFidelityCritical is YES.
SourceExpectedValue remains empty when the key has no direct counterpart or SourceFidelityCritical is NO.
AssertionDomain classifies the engineering role of a concordance candidate.
Allowed AssertionDomain values include PROCESS_CONDITION, UTILITY_CONDITION, PRODUCT_SPEC, EQUIPMENT_LIMIT, OPERATING_TARGET, SCOPE_STATE, LOCATION_STATE, REGULATORY_STATE, and CONTROL_LOGIC.
DiscoverySource records where the candidate came from.
Allowed DiscoverySource values include STRUCTURED_TABLE, METADATA_FIELD, PROSE_EXTRACTION, OPEN_ISSUE, DECISION_LOG, SCOPE_CHANGE, HUMAN_ADDED, SECTION_DISCOVERY, and HYPERGRAPH_AUXILIARY.
Criticality values are HIGH, NORMAL, and LOW.

The Schema Annex covers nine schema families for all 18 canonical CSV files in the _PriceSources library.
The Schema Annex was hardened against the canonical _PriceSources library as of 2026-02-18.
Family 1 standard unit-rate files use header ItemID, Category, Description, Unit, RateMin, RateMax, RecommendedRate, Basis, Confidence, Notes.

Family 1 covers Structural_Concrete_Rates, Building_Envelope_Rates, Mechanical_System_Rates, Electrical_System_Rates, Earthwork_Civil_Rates, Paving_Surfacing_Rates, Underground_Utility_Rates, Fees_Permits_Insurance, and Interior_Architectural_Rates.
Family 1 observed Basis values are MARKET, PARAMETRIC, ALLOWANCE, and N/A.
Family 1 observed Confidence values are HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, and N/A.
Family 1 ESTIMATING guidance uses RecommendedRate as point estimate, records RateMin and RateMax for risk analysis, and flags Confidence=LOW items for vendor quote replacement.
Family 2 Equipment_Pricing.csv uses header ItemID, Category, Description, Unit, PriceMin, PriceMax, RecommendedPrice, Quantity_Assumed, Basis, Confidence, Notes.
Family 2 uses Price columns rather than Rate columns.
Family 2 Quantity_Assumed is present and may be blank for lump-sum items.
Family 3 Optional_Items_Pricing.csv uses header ItemID, Category, Description, Unit, PriceMin, PriceMax, RecommendedPrice, Basis, Confidence, Notes.
Family 3 uses Price columns rather than Rate columns and has no Quantity_Assumed column.
Family 3 options include base scope, alternates, and items pending resolution.
Family 4 Professional_Staff_Rates.csv uses header RoleID, Role, Category, HourlyRate_CAD, Basis, Confidence, Notes.
Family 4 has a single rate per role with no min, max, or recommended pattern.
Family 4 uses Role rather than RoleName.
Family 4 Category groups roles such as Design, Management, Construction, Admin, and Specialty.
Family 4 embeds currency in HourlyRate_CAD.
Family 5 Construction_Labour_Rates.csv uses header TradeID, Trade, HourlyRate_CAD, BurdenMultiplier, FullyBurdenedRate_CAD, Basis, Confidence, Notes.
Family 5 uses a single rate with burden multiplier to produce fully burdened rate.
Family 5 has no min or max pattern and uses TradeID rather than ItemID.
Family 6 Professional_Design_Fees.csv uses header ItemID, Discipline, Description, FeePercentMin, FeePercentMax, RecommendedPercent, FeeBase, Basis, Confidence, Notes.
Family 6 uses Discipline rather than Category.
Family 6 fee percent columns use the min, max, and recommended pattern.
Family 6 FeeBase indicates the percentage basis, such as construction_value.
Family 6 items DF-06, DF-07, and DF-08 use lump_sum in percent fields when the fee is fixed rather than percentage-based.
Family 7 Parametric_Building_Rates.csv uses header ItemID, BuildingType, Description, Unit, RateMin, RateMax, RecommendedRate, Basis, Confidence, Notes.
Family 7 uses BuildingType rather than Category.
Family 7 otherwise follows the standard unit-rate column pattern.
Family 7 is used for parametric cross-checks and fallback estimation.
Family 8 Assumed_Project_Parameters.csv uses header ParameterID, Category, Parameter, Value, Unit, Source, Confidence, Notes.
Family 8 uses Source rather than Basis.
Family 8 has no rate columns and each parameter is a single Value.
Family 8 observed Source values are ASSUMPTION, DESIGN_BASIS, CONFIRMED, DERIVED, and PARAMETRIC.
Family 8 observed Confidence values are HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW.
Family 9 Level of Effort files use header Execution, DeliverableID, DeliverableName, RoleID, Role, EstimatedHours, Basis, Notes.
Family 9 covers Proposal_Level_of_Effort.csv for multi-execution shared use and Level_of_Effort.csv for execution-specific use.
Family 9 has no Confidence column because provenance is conveyed through Basis alone.
Family 9 requires all columns, including Execution, DeliverableName, and Role.
Family 9 observed Basis value is PARAMETRIC.
HIGH confidence means human-confirmed, vendor-quoted, or source-document-derived.
MEDIUM confidence means a parametric market rate or comparable-project benchmark.
LOW confidence means an allowance or assumption-based placeholder.
Override_Log.csv minimum columns are OverrideID, File, Key, Field, PriorValue, PriorConfidence, PriorBasis or PriorSource, NewValue, NewConfidence, NewBasis or NewSource, HumanSource, and Notes.
Conflicts.csv schema includes ConflictID, Key, Description, Contenders, ProposedAuthority, HumanRuling, and Notes.

When TASK and the skill disagree about write authorization or tool use, the narrower instruction wins.
A run report must surface contradictions between TASK and skill authorization.
Instruction conflicts must be reported rather than silently reconciled.
If DECOMP_VARIANT is absent, semantic-matrix-build defaults it to PROJECT and reports that default.
If ADVANCE_ON_PASS requests _STATUS.md editing without authorization, semantic-matrix-build does not edit status.
semantic-matrix-build reads only inside deliverable_folder except for the decomposition document used for traceability.
semantic-matrix-build reads _CONTEXT.md, _STATUS.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, MEMORY.md, and production documents in that order when present.
Missing production documents are recorded as absent and do not fail the run.
semantic-matrix-build must not read sibling deliverable folders.
semantic-matrix-build may write only inside deliverable_folder.
semantic-matrix-build may overwrite _SEMANTIC.md as its primary output.
semantic-matrix-build may write _STATUS.md only if STATUS_POLICY requires it and TASK authorizes it.
semantic-matrix-build never modifies production documents or deliverable metadata files other than authorized _STATUS.md.
_SEMANTIC.md includes a one to three sentence Perspective near the top.
The Perspective names what the deliverable is for at a semantic level.
The Perspective identifies the kinds of knowledge the lens must carry.
The Perspective includes relevant source-state caveats at a category level when present.
The Perspective avoids engineering correctness claims.
The Perspective avoids exact code clauses, event-name lists, file paths, line numbers, implementation paths, and other particulars.
Final matrix cells must be deliverable-conditioned.
Final matrix cells must be category-level rather than requirement-level.
Final matrix cells must be one phrase only.
Final matrix cells must be two to five words.
Final matrix cells must be free of row and column axis labels.
Final matrix cells must be free of algebra symbols, unresolved plus signs, and raw formula text.
Semantic multiplication combines two semantic units into their intersection.
Semantic addition groups terms into a collection.
Semantic addition must not leak into final cell values.
Every list-valued cell must be interpreted into one atomic semantic unit.
Every interpreted cell must show exactly three interpretation steps.
Step 1 computes and resolves the axis product a = r times c.
Step 2 computes and resolves every contributor projection.
Step 3 selects one final cell phrase.
The Step 3 final phrase captures the shared semantic core of all resolved projections.
Matrix A canonical values must be used exactly and not edited.
Matrix A normative-guiding cell is prescriptive direction.
Matrix A normative-applying cell is mandatory practice.
Matrix A normative-judging cell is compliance determination.
Matrix A normative-reviewing cell is regulatory audit.
Matrix A operative-guiding cell is procedural direction.
Matrix A operative-applying cell is practical execution.
Matrix A operative-judging cell is performance assessment.
Matrix A operative-reviewing cell is process audit.
Matrix A evaluative-guiding cell is value orientation.
Matrix A evaluative-applying cell is merit application.
Matrix A evaluative-judging cell is worth determination.
Matrix A evaluative-reviewing cell is quality appraisal.
Matrix B canonical values must be used exactly and not edited.
Matrix B data-necessity cell is essential fact.
Matrix B data-sufficiency cell is adequate evidence.
Matrix B data-completeness cell is comprehensive record.
Matrix B data-consistency cell is reliable measurement.
Matrix B information-necessity cell is essential signal.
Matrix B information-sufficiency cell is adequate context.
Matrix B information-completeness cell is comprehensive account.
Matrix B information-consistency cell is coherent message.
Matrix B knowledge-necessity cell is fundamental understanding.
Matrix B knowledge-sufficiency cell is competent expertise.
Matrix B knowledge-completeness cell is thorough mastery.
Matrix B knowledge-consistency cell is coherent understanding.
Matrix B wisdom-necessity cell is essential discernment.
Matrix B wisdom-sufficiency cell is adequate judgment.
Matrix B wisdom-completeness cell is holistic insight.
Matrix B wisdom-consistency cell is principled reasoning.
Matrix C uses L_C(i,j) as the sum over A(i,k) times B(k,j).
Matrix C uses C(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_C(i,j)).
Matrix F uses L_F(i,j) as the sum over C(i,k) times B(k,j).
Matrix F uses F(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_F(i,j)).
Matrix D uses L_D(i,j) = A(i,j) plus resolution times F(i,j).
Matrix D uses D(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_D(i,j)).
Matrix D uses exactly two contributors: the A cell and the resolution-transformed F cell.
Matrix K is the transpose of D with K(i,j) = D(j,i).
Matrix G is created by removing the wisdom row from Matrix B.
Matrix X uses L_X(i,j) as the sum over K(i,k) times G(k,j).
Matrix X uses X(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_X(i,j)).
Matrix T is the transpose of B with T(i,j) = B(j,i).
Matrix E uses L_E(i,j) as the sum over X(i,k) times T(k,j).
Matrix E uses E(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_E(i,j)).
_SEMANTIC.md must be written in the prescribed order.
Matrix Z is a delimiter that prevents summary tables from being parsed as Matrix E result work.
Matrix Z is not a semantic matrix.
Inputs Read SourceRefs use path anchors, not present, absent, or location TBD forms.
An input must not be claimed as read unless it was actually read.
Before reporting success, semantic-matrix-build audits every Result table and every Matrix Summary table.
If audit fails after writing _SEMANTIC.md, the file header is marked Audit: FAIL.
If audit fails, semantic-matrix-build does not repair and re-audit in the same run.
With PRESERVE_CURRENT, semantic-matrix-build does not change lifecycle state and records preservation by runtime policy.
With ADVANCE_ON_PASS, semantic-matrix-build sets or verifies SEMANTIC_READY only when _STATUS.md editing is authorized.
With NO_STATUS_TOUCH, semantic-matrix-build does not edit _STATUS.md.

The TASK run report includes run status, deliverable identity, resolved folder, variant, semantic path, audit result, status action, validator result, missing inputs, failing cells, and production document safety.
When the validator exists and tool use is permitted, semantic-matrix-build runs tools/validation/validate_semantic_matrix.py on deliverable_folder.
If the validator is unavailable, semantic-matrix-build reports validator not available and does not claim validator PASS.
When invoked for DOMAIN, semantic-matrix-build reads Knowledge Type non-metadata markdown documents and uses DOMAIN terminology while keeping the matrix algebra unchanged.
semantic-matrix-build tool posture is reasoning-first.
Deterministic tools are used only for validation and filesystem safety when available.
The preferred tool sequence starts by reading files inside ScopePath needed by the skill.
The preferred tool sequence generates _SEMANTIC.md by reasoning from the skill contract.
The preferred tool sequence runs the semantic audit specified in QA_CHECKS.md.
validate_semantic_matrix.py is required in normal repo runs when available and permitted.
validate_semantic_pipeline_scope.py is required when project ORCHESTRATOR policy calls for it and the tool is available.
If a validator is unavailable, semantic-matrix-build reports unavailable and does not claim validator PASS.
Reasoning is required for deriving the deliverable perspective.
Reasoning is required for choosing deliverable-conditioned but non-literal semantic phrases.
Reasoning is required for resolving each axis anchor.
Reasoning is required for resolving every projected contributor in Step 2.
Reasoning is required for selecting centroid attractors.
Reasoning is required for auditing final cells for semantic product validity.
Tools or scripts must not be used to bypass semantic reasoning work.
semantic-matrix-build must not claim cross-deliverable conclusions.
semantic-matrix-build must not claim engineering correctness.
semantic-matrix-build must not claim validator PASS unless the validator actually ran.
The normal write target for semantic-matrix-build is deliverable_folder/_SEMANTIC.md.
_STATUS.md is a conditional write target only when status policy requires it and TASK authorization allows it.
When the validator is unavailable, semantic-matrix-build completes semantic audit manually and reports validator unavailable.
When _CONTEXT.md is missing, semantic-matrix-build fails with FAILED_INPUTS.
When a production document is missing, semantic-matrix-build records absent and continues.
When a status edit is requested but unauthorized, semantic-matrix-build does not edit _STATUS.md and reports the contradiction.
When tool output contradicts file content, semantic-matrix-build reports the discrepancy and does not hide it.
When a brief asks for out-of-scope writes, semantic-matrix-build refuses those writes and reports a scope violation.
